answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond for one bridge tower slot with a key-bound cedar frame serial on the register. Each epoch it posts a signed nebula transit time; auditors recompute it from the ephemeris and burn the bond for a miss over two minutes or a reused serial. Slot fees rise: first 34 credits, kth 34+6(k-1), 1000th 6028, so 1,000 fakes pay 3,031,000 in fees plus 70,000 locked. A rented ring fails: a rented cedar frame carries its owner's serial, so a second key on it is rejected and both bonds burn. An honest observer pays 104 once and recovers the bond after audit.
